# Adjudication Task — Chapter 323

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃323화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그 모든 일은 찰나에 일어났다.
  6|
  7|대기에 스며들어 있던 기운이 요동쳤고, 탁자에 기대 놓았던 검이 한 사람의 손아귀를 향해 빨려 들어갔다.
  8|
  9|그리고…….
 10|
 11|슈아아악!
 12|
 13|눈부신 빛줄기가 눈 앞을 가렸다. 더할 나위 없이 빠르고 정확한 일격.
 14|
 15|검신을 감싼 푸른 기운의 결정체가 휘황한 빛을 뿌린다. 그 빛을 부르는 또 다른 이름을, 나는 이미 알고 있다.
 16|
 17|‘검강(劍罡).’
 18|
 19|초절정이라는 위대한 경지에 발을 디딘 자들에게 허락된 권능. 세상에 존재하는 어느 것보다 강력한 그것이 내 정수리를 향해 떨어지고 있었다.
 20|
 21|이대로라면 죽는다. 틀림없이 죽을 것이다.
 22|
 23|하지만.
 24|
 25|‘이 정도로는 어림도 없지.’
 26|
 27|한없이 느려진 세상 속, 내가 움직임과 동시에 검강이 허공을 갈랐다.
 28|
 29|서걱! 콰아아아!
 30|
 31|모든 것이 갈라졌다. 탁자도, 의자도, 오랜 세월 이 자리를 지키고 있었을 다루의 바닥도.
 32|
 33|뒤이어 검강이 불러온 광풍이 주위를 휩쓸었다. 사람들의 비명과 굉음이 사방을 집어삼킨다. 그 너머로 노인의 부릅뜬 눈동자가 보였다.
 34|
 35|“네, 네놈이 어떻게…….”
 36|
 37|나는 순간적으로 품에 끌어안았던 주화란을 부드럽게 옆으로 밀어 내며 대답했다.
 38|
 39|“어떻게 피하긴. 보이니까 피한 거 아니겠습니까.”
 40|
 41|“……!”
 42|
 43|“사람들이 그러더라고요. 초절정은, 검강은 인외(人外)의 영역이라고.”
 44|
 45|황보엄의 주름진 얼굴 위로 감출 수 없는 충격이 드리운다.
 46|
 47|“그, 그렇다면 설마 네놈이……!”
 48|
 49|“글쎄요.”
 50|
 51|흐릿한 미소로 대답을 대신했다. 지금쯤 황보엄의 머릿속에는 벼락이 치고 있을 것이다.
 52|
 53|물론 나는 아직 초절정의 경지에 오를 만한 깨달음을 얻지 못했다.
 54|
 55|정확히 말하자면, 무공이 아닌 신체의 능력 자체가 인외의 경지에 올라 있다고 해야 옳겠지.
 56|
 57|‘이걸 뭐라고 해야 하나.’
 58|
 59|초절정 고수(물리)?
 60|
 61|무림 역사상 전무후무한, 새로운 형태의 초절정 고수인 것은 분명하다.
 62|
 63|나는 어깨를 으쓱하며 말했다.
 64|
 65|“별거 아닙니다. 하니까 되던데요.”
 66|
 67|황보엄이 핏발 선 눈으로 외쳤다.
 68|
 69|“믿을 수 없다! 너 같은 어린놈이 어찌 그와 같은 경지에 오를 수 있단 말이냐!”
 70|
 71|“믿을 수 없는 건 이쪽도 마찬가집니다. 세상에, 이런 자리에서 검을 휘두르다니. 제정신이세요?”
 72|
 73|“그건…….”
 74|
 75|덜컥 굳은 황보엄의 눈동자가 좌중을 훑었다.
 76|
 77|다행히 나만을 정확히 노렸기에 다친 사람은 없었지만, 그들 모두의 얼굴에는 경악과 분노가 떠올라 있었다.
 78|
 79|“정파가 어쩌고, 대종남파가 어쩌고 하더니 꼭지 한 번 도니까 마두가 따로 없네. 차라리 이참에 종간나 파로 이름 바꾸는 게 어떻습니까.”
 80|
 81|“놈……!”
 82|
 83|검 자루를 쥔 황보엄의 손아귀가 부르르 떨렸다. 주위를 둘러보며 갈등하던 그의 눈동자가 차갑게 가라앉았다.
 84|
 85|“종남파의 제자들은 명을 받들라.”
 86|
 87|“예, 옛!”
 88|
 89|갑자기 벌어진 사태에 석상처럼 굳어 있던 서른 명의 태을검대가 퍼뜩 정신을 차렸다.
 90|
 91|황급히 포권을 취하는 그들의 머리 위로 황보엄의 명령이 떨어졌다.
 92|
 93|“지금 즉시 출입구를 봉쇄하라. 그 누구도 이 자리를 벗어나서는 안 될 것이다.”
 94|
 95|“사, 사숙!”
 96|
 97|“그, 그것은…….”
 98|
 99|“무엇 하느냐! 노부의 명을 어길 셈이더냐!”
100|
101|황보엄이 노호성에 태을검대가 멈칫거리던 그때, 나직한 목소리가 모두의 귓가를 파고들었다.
102|
103|“예, 어길 셈입니다.”
104|
105|목소리의 주인을 확인한 황보엄의 얼굴에 노기가 서렸다.
106|
107|“혁소평, 네놈이 감히…….”
108|
109|낯익은 녀석이었다. 종남일룡 혁소평.
110|
111|그는 형용할 수 없이 복잡한 눈빛으로 황보엄을 응시하며 말했다.
112|
113|“멈추십시오. 처음이자 마지막으로 간청드립니다.”
114|
115|“무어라?”
116|
117|“이건, 지금 사숙께서 보이는 모습은…… 대종남파의 제자가 할 짓이 아니지 않습니까.”
118|
119|“닥치지 못할까!”
120|
121|콰아아아!
122|
123|다시 한번 휘몰아친 광풍에 혁소평의 몸이 주르륵 밀려났다.
124|
125|그러나 녀석의 눈빛은 흔들리지 않았다.
126|
127|그런 혁소평과 머뭇거리는 서른 명의 태을검대를 번갈아 바라보던 황보엄이 입술을 질끈 깨물었다.
128|
129|“이, 이놈들이.”
130|
131|그리고 다음 순간, 황보엄이 품에서 자그마한 동패(銅牌)를 꺼내어 혁소평의 발아래에 던졌다.
132|
133|“네 사부가 노부에게 맡기고 간 본문의 장문령부이니라. 이래도 거부할 생각이더냐?”
134|
135|“……!”
136|
137|장문령부는 한 문파의 정점에 선 강력한 권위의 상징.
138|
139|스승의 동패를 확인한 혁소평의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
140|
141|“사숙께서는, 참으로 여전하십니다.”
142|
143|“양자택일해라. 파문(破門)인지, 아니면 존명(尊命)인지.”
144|
145|“파문…….”
146|
147|혁소평의 회한 어린 시선이 나와 주화란에게 닿았다.
148|
149|이내 쓴웃음을 지은 그가 동패를 향해 큰절과 함께 머리를 찧었다.
150|
151|쿵! 쿵! 쿵!
152|
153|“제자 혁소평, 장문령부의 명을 받드옵니다!”
154|
155|피를 토하는 듯한 외침. 찢어진 이마에서는 핏줄기가 흐른다.
156|
157|아무 고통도 느끼지 못하는 듯한 무표정으로 자리에서 일어난 혁소평이 다루의 입구를 막아섰다. 서른 명의 태을검대 또한 마찬가지였다.
158|
159|이 모든 상황을 지켜본 내가 혀를 찼다.
160|
161|“이 정도면 선을 넘은 게 아니라, 아예 지우셨는데? 이거 뒷감당 되겠습니까?”
162|
163|이 자리에는 화산파와 개방, 하오문의 주요 인사들이 모여 있다. 제아무리 종남파라고 하지만 오늘의 후폭풍은 거셀 터.
164|
165|그러나 이미 꼭지가 돌아 버린 황보엄의 눈에는 분노만이 가득했다.
166|
167|“저들은 무사할 것이다. 단, 네놈을 제외하고 말이지.”
168|
169|“아하. 우선 나부터 처리하고 뒷수습을 하시겠다?”
170|
171|“그래. 드디어 네놈의 주둥이를 찢을 수 있게 되었구나.”
172|
173|“왜 이렇게 못 찢어서 안달이 나셨을까, 우리 영감님. 태원진가와 열화문이 무슨 빙다리 핫바지도 아니고.”
174|
175|“열화문?”
176|
177|황보엄의 입가에 비웃음이 맺혔다.
178|
179|그리고 다음 순간. 한 줄기 전음이 내 귓가를 파고들었다.
180|
181|- 새끼 호랑이가 위기에 처했건만, 대호(大虎)는 깨어날 줄 모르는구나.
182|
183|“……!”
184|
185|- 노부가 모를 줄 알았더냐, 어리석은 아해야. 내 이미 화왕의 병세가 깊음을 알고 있었느니라.
186|
187|극소수만 알고 있었던 비밀이 새어 나갔다.
188|
189|나도 모르게 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다. 그런 나를 보는 황보엄의 웃음이 짙어졌다.
190|
191|- 화왕 적천강, 그리고 네놈. 참으로 지긋지긋했지. 이참에 열화문과의 악연을 깨끗이 정리하는 것도 나쁘지 않겠군.
192|
193|악연을 정리한다고?
194|
195|황보엄의 한마디에 문득 멍해졌다.
196|
197|지금 내가 생각하고 있는 그것이 맞나?
198|
199|복잡했던 머릿속이 일순간 깔끔하게 비워졌다. 그리고 하나의 생각만이 남았다.
200|
201|“미안한데…… 모두에게 부탁 하나만 합시다.”
202|
203|보이지 않아도 느껴진다.
204|
205|백무성과 청풍, 궁기방과 흑걸개, 월화와 혁무진. 마지막으로 주화란까지. 이 자리에 있는 모든 이들의 시선이 나를 향하고 있었다.
206|
207|그리고 다음 순간, 내 것이라고는 믿기지 않을 만큼 건조한 목소리가 입술 사이로 흘러나왔다.
208|
209|“입구를 막아. 누구도 빠져나가지 못하게.”
210|
211|먼저 입구를 막은 것은 황보엄이지만, 그 문을 열고 닫는 것은 내가 될 것이다.
212|
213|“태을무정검 황보엄.”
214|
215|나는 나직이 한숨을 내쉬었다. 단전에서 끓어오른 극양의 기운이 하얀 김이 되어 흘러나온다.
216|
217|“당신…… 하지 말아야 할 말을 했어.”
218|
219|고작 이 정도로 적천강을 입에 올려서는 안 됐다.
220|
221|정말 그래서는 안 되는 거였다.
222|
223|하지 말아야 할 말을 한 대가는, 지금부터 치르게 될 것이다.
224|
225|“들어와, 이 좆 같은 늙은이야.”
226|
227|찰나를 쪼개고 쪼갠 시간 속, 황보엄과 나는 서로를 향해 쇄도했다.
228|
229|콰아아아아!
230|
231|
232|
233|* * *
234|
235|
236|
237|천하삼십육검(天下三十六劍).
238|
239|천지 사방을 뒤덮은 검기의 그물은 촘촘하고 강대했다.
240|
241|일 년 전 상대했던 노호검객과 전날의 혁소평과는 비교도 되지 않는 검초가 쉬지 않고 뻗어 나온다.
242|
243|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
244|
245|눈이 부실 만큼 빠르고 파괴적이다. 스치기만 해도 살과 뼈가 갈라지고 죽음에 이르게 될 터였다.
246|
247|이건 피할 수 없다. 피할 수 없었다.
248|
249|‘그랬겠지. 일 년 전의 나였다면.’
250|
251|괄목상대(刮目相對)라는 말이 생각난다.
252|
253|눈을 비비고 다시 볼 정도로 뛰어난 성취를 뜻하는 그 말조차도 내게는 부족하다.
254|
255|혹독하고도 끊임없는 수련의 나날 속에서 나는 강해졌다. 아니, 그건 진화라고 해도 무방했다.
256|
257|
258|
259|‘하늘도 무심하시지. 어찌 너 같은 놈이 있을 수 있단 말이냐?’
260|
261|
262|
263|허탈함이 가득한 적천강의 얼굴이 검기의 그물 위로 덧씌워진다.
264|
265|나는 나직하게 웃으며 창, 백염(白炎)을 그어 올렸다.
266|
267|촤아아악!
268|
269|백염의 창날에 어린 극양의 기운이 그물을 찢었다.
270|
271|물고기는 찢어진 그물 사이로 도망치겠지만, 나는 물고기가 아닌 한 마리의 상어였다. 그물을 던진 어부는 그 사실을 간과했음이 분명하다.
272|
273|늙은 어부의 주름진 얼굴에는 경악으로 가득했다.
274|
275|“너-!”
276|
277|나는 대답하지 않았다. 무릎을 굽히고, 허리를 숙였다. 손에 들린 창이 용의 꼬리처럼 부드럽게 휘어졌다.
278|
279|‘화룡일미(火龍一尾).’
280|
281|화아아악! 꽈앙!
282|
283|푸르게 타오르는 창과 검이 부딪친다. 굉음과 함께 막대한 기파가 뿜어져 나온다.
284|
285|힘을 아끼고자 했던 걸까. 그랬다면 황보엄의 선택은 단단히 어긋났다. 아무리 공력의 소모가 극심했어도 검강을 사용했어야 옳다.
286|
287|“흡!”
288|
289|부릅뜬 눈. 인외의 경지에 접어든 근력과 무공 본연이 가진 난폭함에 노인의 신형이 휘청인다.
290|
291|“이, 이게 무슨 무공……!”
292|
293|열화문의 개파사조는 당대의 천하제일이라 불렸다.
294|
295|그는 열화신공을 창안하여 문파의 뿌리로 삼았고, 그 뒤를 이은 열여섯 명의 문주들은 열화신공이라는 뿌리로 각기 다른 가지가 되었다.
296|
297|화룡신창(火龍神槍)도 마찬가지였다. 5대 문주가 창안한 이 창술은 극도로 파괴적이고 거칠었다. 그야말로 화룡의 움직임과 같다.
298|
299|그리고…….
300|
301|‘이제 시작이야.’
302|
303|후우우웅!
304|
305|나는 힘을 아끼지 않았다. 찌르고, 베고, 휘두르는 동시에 때렸다.
306|
307|푸른 화염이 난폭하게 날뛸 때마다 하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음이 천지를 울렸다.
308|
309|‘꼬리 다음은 발톱이다.’
310|

*—The young tiger is in danger, yet the great tiger shows no sign of waking.*

“……!”

[P92]
*—Did you think this old man wouldn’t know, you foolish child? I already knew the Fire King’s illness was grave.*

[P93]

[P94]

[P95]
*—The Fire King Jeok Cheongang, and you. I have had more than enough of you both. This might be a good opportunity to settle my bad blood with the Fire Gate Clan once and for all.*

[P96]
Settle his bad blood?

[P97]
Hwangbo Eom’s words left me momentarily dazed.

[P98]
*Does he mean what I think he means?*

[P99]
My tangled thoughts vanished in an instant. Only one remained.

[P100]
“Sorry, but I need to ask everyone a favor.”

[P101]
I could feel their gazes even without looking.

[P102]
Baek Museong and Cheongpung. Gung Gibang and Heukgeol Beggar. Wolhwa and Hyuk Mujin. And finally, Ju Hwaran.

[P103]
Everyone in the room was looking at me.

[P104]
Then a voice so dry that I could hardly believe it belonged to me slipped between my lips.

[P105]
“Block the entrance. Don’t let anyone get out.”

[P106]
Hwangbo Eom had been the first to block the door, but I would be the one to decide when it opened and closed.

[P107]
“Taeeul Merciless Sword Hwangbo Eom.”

[P108]
I let out a quiet sigh. Extreme Yang qi boiled up from my dantian and flowed from me as white steam.

[P109]
“You… said something you never should have.”

[P110]
He should never have brought up Jeok Cheongang over something as trivial as this.

[P111]
He truly shouldn’t have.

[P112]
Starting now, he would pay the price for saying what should never have been said.

[P113]
“Come at me, you fucking old bastard.”

[P114]
In time split into smaller and smaller instants, Hwangbo Eom and I rushed toward each other.

[P115]
Kraaaaaash!

[P116]
* * *

[P117]
Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords.

[P118]
A dense and powerful net of Sword Energy covered heaven and earth in every direction.

[P119]
The sword forms came without pause, on a completely different level from those of the Roaring Fury Swordsman I had faced a year ago or Hyuk Sopyung the day before.

[P120]
Shishishishishik!

[P121]
They were blindingly fast and destructive. Even a glancing blow would split flesh and bone and bring death.

[P122]
*I can’t dodge this. There’s no way.*

[P123]
*Or there wouldn’t have been a year ago.*

[P124]
The saying *wipe your eyes and look again* came to mind—a phrase for progress so astonishing that you had to rub your eyes and take another look.

[P125]
Even that fell short of describing me.

[P126]
Through endless days of brutal training, I had grown stronger. No, it would not be wrong to call it evolution.

[P127]
*Heaven is truly heartless. How can someone like you even exist?*

[P128]
Jeok Cheongang’s face, filled with helpless disbelief, appeared over the net of Sword Energy.

[P129]
I laughed quietly and swept my spear, White Flame, upward.

[P130]
Shraaaak!

[P131]
The Extreme Yang qi coating White Flame’s spearhead tore through the net.

[P132]
A fish would have fled through the gap in the torn net, but I was no fish.

[P133]
I was a shark.

[P134]
The fisherman who had cast the net had clearly overlooked that fact.

[P135]
The old fisherman’s wrinkled face filled with shock.

[P136]
“You—!”

[P137]
I did not answer.

[P138]
I bent my knees and lowered my body. The spear in my hand curved smoothly like a dragon’s tail.

[P139]
*Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.*

[P140]
Fwoooosh! Boom!

[P141]

[P142]
Had Hwangbo Eom been trying to conserve his strength?

[P143]

[P144]
“Hup!”

[P145]
His eyes opened wide.

[P146]
The old man staggered before my strength, which had entered the realm beyond humanity, and the innate ferocity of my martial art.

[P147]
“Wh-what kind of martial art is this…?”

[P149]
He created the Fire Gate Divine Technique and made it the root of the clan. The sixteen Sect Leaders who followed became different branches growing from that same root.

[P150]
The Fire Dragon Divine Spear was no different.

[P151]

[P152]
And…

[P153]
*This is only the beginning.*

[P154]
Whoooosh!

[P155]
I held nothing back.

[P156]
I thrust, slashed, swept, and struck.

[P157]
Whenever the blue flames ran wild, thunderous crashes like the sky splitting apart shook heaven and earth.

[P158]
*After the tail come the claws.*

[P159]
No one under heaven had ever seen a dragon fight.

[P160]
But while learning the Fire Dragon Divine Spear, I had found myself wondering.

[P161]
*If a fire dragon really swung its claws, wouldn’t it look exactly like this?*

[P162]
Gooooong.

[P163]
Extreme Yang qi coiled around the tip of my spear.

[P164]
The tea spilled across the floor during Hwangbo Eom’s earlier rampage had long since evaporated. The jade-colored tea set glowed red-hot, as if it were back inside the kiln where it had been fired.

[P165]
Sensing the danger, Hwangbo Eom roared like thunder.

[P166]
“You bastard!”

[P167]
He was already nearing eighty.

[P168]
But to someone who had entered the Supreme Peak realm, age was nothing more than a number.

[P169]
His formidable internal energy and the Zhongnan Sect’s ultimate techniques, honed for more than a jiazi, poured down like beams of light.

[P170]
Swoooosh!

[P171]
If the Heavenly River Thirty-Six Swords were a net, this was a harpoon meant to finish its prey.

[P172]
As his sword slashed toward my chest at incredible speed, scattering dozens of afterimages, one martial art flashed through my mind.

[P173]
*Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword.*

[P174]
One of the Zhongnan Sect’s most celebrated ultimate sword techniques.

[P175]
Jeok Cheongang had described the Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword as a sword art of extreme speed.

[P176]
Then he had added one more thing.

[P177]
*Maybe this old man is going senile. Why do I get the feeling you’ll be faster than the sword?*

[P178]
If Jeok Cheongang woke up, I wanted to tell him he had been right.

[P179]
And that the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts had shattered the Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword.

[P180]
*Heavenly Strike.*

[P181]
The fire dragon swung its claws.

[P182]
The strike descended from the sky, erasing the afterimages created by the Taeeul Light-Dividing Sword as it fell like a bolt of lightning.

[P183]
Kraaaaaash!

[P184]
A pillar of hellfire erupted.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 323

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃323화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그 모든 일은 찰나에 일어났다.
  6|
  7|대기에 스며들어 있던 기운이 요동쳤고, 탁자에 기대 놓았던 검이 한 사람의 손아귀를 향해 빨려 들어갔다.
  8|
  9|그리고…….
 10|
 11|슈아아악!
 12|
 13|눈부신 빛줄기가 눈 앞을 가렸다. 더할 나위 없이 빠르고 정확한 일격.
 14|
 15|검신을 감싼 푸른 기운의 결정체가 휘황한 빛을 뿌린다. 그 빛을 부르는 또 다른 이름을, 나는 이미 알고 있다.
 16|
 17|‘검강(劍罡).’
 18|
 19|초절정이라는 위대한 경지에 발을 디딘 자들에게 허락된 권능. 세상에 존재하는 어느 것보다 강력한 그것이 내 정수리를 향해 떨어지고 있었다.
 20|
 21|이대로라면 죽는다. 틀림없이 죽을 것이다.
 22|
 23|하지만.
 24|
 25|‘이 정도로는 어림도 없지.’
 26|
 27|한없이 느려진 세상 속, 내가 움직임과 동시에 검강이 허공을 갈랐다.
 28|
 29|서걱! 콰아아아!
 30|
 31|모든 것이 갈라졌다. 탁자도, 의자도, 오랜 세월 이 자리를 지키고 있었을 다루의 바닥도.
 32|
 33|뒤이어 검강이 불러온 광풍이 주위를 휩쓸었다. 사람들의 비명과 굉음이 사방을 집어삼킨다. 그 너머로 노인의 부릅뜬 눈동자가 보였다.
 34|
 35|“네, 네놈이 어떻게…….”
 36|
 37|나는 순간적으로 품에 끌어안았던 주화란을 부드럽게 옆으로 밀어 내며 대답했다.
 38|
 39|“어떻게 피하긴. 보이니까 피한 거 아니겠습니까.”
 40|
 41|“……!”
 42|
 43|“사람들이 그러더라고요. 초절정은, 검강은 인외(人外)의 영역이라고.”
 44|
 45|황보엄의 주름진 얼굴 위로 감출 수 없는 충격이 드리운다.
 46|
 47|“그, 그렇다면 설마 네놈이……!”
 48|
 49|“글쎄요.”
 50|
 51|흐릿한 미소로 대답을 대신했다. 지금쯤 황보엄의 머릿속에는 벼락이 치고 있을 것이다.
 52|
 53|물론 나는 아직 초절정의 경지에 오를 만한 깨달음을 얻지 못했다.
 54|
 55|정확히 말하자면, 무공이 아닌 신체의 능력 자체가 인외의 경지에 올라 있다고 해야 옳겠지.
 56|
 57|‘이걸 뭐라고 해야 하나.’
 58|
 59|초절정 고수(물리)?
 60|
 61|무림 역사상 전무후무한, 새로운 형태의 초절정 고수인 것은 분명하다.
 62|
 63|나는 어깨를 으쓱하며 말했다.
 64|
 65|“별거 아닙니다. 하니까 되던데요.”
 66|
 67|황보엄이 핏발 선 눈으로 외쳤다.
 68|
 69|“믿을 수 없다! 너 같은 어린놈이 어찌 그와 같은 경지에 오를 수 있단 말이냐!”
 70|
 71|“믿을 수 없는 건 이쪽도 마찬가집니다. 세상에, 이런 자리에서 검을 휘두르다니. 제정신이세요?”
 72|
 73|“그건…….”
 74|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
